question: Which goods break first when a crisis hits Luxembourg's exports, and which import is critical?
title: Luxembourg Trade Crisis Impact on Goods
approach: This chain identifies which export goods break first during crises by analyzing changes in export values during crisis years, then identifies the critical import by ranking imports in the latest year. It compares crisis years with their preceding years to detect breaks in exports and ranks imports to find critical goods.

steps.question: Which export goods experienced the largest declines in value between 2008 and 2009 in Luxembourg?
steps.purpose: To identify which export goods broke first during the 2008 financial crisis by showing the largest export value declines between 2008 and 2009.
steps.queried: exports · by HS2 product (top 10) · 2008–2009 · change between the two years
steps.note: Iron and steel exports had the largest decline between 2008 and 2009, falling by 1.29 billion euros (−48.4%).

steps.question: Which export goods experienced the largest declines in value between 2019 and 2020 in Luxembourg?
steps.purpose: To identify which export goods broke first during the COVID-19 crisis by showing the largest export value declines between 2019 and 2020.
steps.queried: exports · by HS2 product (top 10) · 2019–2020 · change between the two years
steps.note: Electrical machinery and equipment exports fell sharply between 2019 and 2020 by 1.49 billion euros (−70.0%), while iron and steel also declined by 404.7 million euros (−26.0%).

steps.question: Which export goods experienced the largest declines in value between 2022 and 2023 in Luxembourg?
steps.purpose: To identify which export goods broke first during the 2022 energy price shock aftershock by showing the largest export value declines between 2022 and 2023.
steps.queried: exports · by HS2 product (top 10) · 2022–2023 · change between the two years
steps.note: Between 2022 and 2023, iron and steel exports declined by 514.9 million euros (−27.1%), the largest fall among the top 10 export goods.

steps.question: What were the top 10 import goods by value in Luxembourg in 2025?
steps.purpose: To identify the critical import goods by ranking the largest import goods by value in the latest complete year 2025.
steps.queried: imports · by HS2 product (top 10) · 2025 · value in €
steps.note: Vehicles and parts were the largest import good in 2025 at 3.32 billion euros, representing 13.2% of total imports.

steps.question: What were the yearly export values of Iron and steel in Luxembourg from 2007 to 2010?
steps.purpose: Steps 1 and 2 show Iron and steel had the largest export value declines during the 2008 and 2020 crises, so a yearly series around the 2008 crisis will clarify the timing and extent of the break.
steps.note: Iron and steel exports peaked at 2.67 billion euros in 2008 and declined to 1.80 billion euros by 2010.

steps.question: What were the yearly import values of Vehicles and parts in Luxembourg from 2020 to 2025?
steps.purpose: Step 4 shows Vehicles and parts as the top import good by value in 2025, so a yearly series will show its trend and criticality over recent years.
steps.note: Vehicles and parts imports increased from 2.81 billion euros in 2020 to 3.32 billion euros in 2025, peaking at 3.64 billion euros in 2024.

headline: Iron and steel exports break first during crises in Luxembourg, while vehicles and parts are the most critical import.

points.text: Iron and steel exports experienced the largest declines during the 2008 financial crisis, falling from 2.67 billion euros in 2008 to 1.38 billion euros in 2009, and also showed a significant decline during the COVID-19 crisis and the 2022 energy price shock aftershock, indicating they break first in crises.

Electrical machinery and equipment exports showed a large increase during the 2008 crisis but suffered the largest decline during the COVID-19 crisis, dropping from 2.12 billion euros in 2019 to 637.4 million euros in 2020, highlighting variability in which goods break first depending on the crisis.

During the 2022–2023 period, several export goods declined, including iron and steel, aluminium, plastics, and paper, but iron and steel had the largest fall among them, confirming its vulnerability in crises.

Vehicles and parts are the largest import good in Luxembourg in 2025, valued at 3.32 billion euros and representing 13.2% of total imports, with imports increasing steadily from 2.81 billion euros in 2020 to a peak of 3.64 billion euros in 2024, underscoring their critical role in imports.

conclusion: Iron and steel exports consistently break first during major crises in Luxembourg, showing the largest declines in export value during the 2008 financial crisis, the COVID-19 crisis, and the 2022 energy price shock aftershock. Electrical machinery and equipment exports also show significant fluctuations but are less consistent. Vehicles and parts stand out as the most critical import good by value, with a steady increase in imports over recent years. This analysis does not cover the causes behind these patterns or the impact on other sectors, and it is limited to the goods and years covered in the data.
